reason: R2 is just a pull-up/load for the VOUT1 branch; removing it doesn’t inherently break the biasing/current-steering devices, but VOUT1 will no longer have a defined pull-up path and may float or sit near VSS depending on leakage. Caveat: if you still need a usable VOUT1, replace R2 with another load (current source/active load) or ensure the next stage provides the load.
impact_estimate: Low if VOUT1 is not required as a defined output; moderate if VOUT1 must be a valid output

reason: Same role as R2 but for VOUT2; deleting it keeps the core bias devices (M4/M2) intact but removes the defined pull-up/load at the output node. Caveat: you’ll need an alternative load to define VOUT2 level, gain, and swing.
impact_estimate: Low if VOUT2 is not required as a defined output; moderate if VOUT2 must be a valid output

reason: M0 appears to be a PMOS bias/current-source device that sets the IB1 branch current (gated by VIN1); if you only need the other branch to function (or you can provide IB1 externally), M0 can be removed without destroying the remaining branch’s operation. Caveat: IB1 will be undefined without M0, so you must supply a replacement bias/current for IB1 if the VOUT1 branch is still needed.
impact_estimate: Low-to-moderate (removes one branch’s bias source; other branch can still operate, but IB1 needs replacement if used)
